fichas.title: Typology: spatial structures and volumes
fichas.summary: Building typology is a three-dimensional spatial theme shaped by function, construction, and town-planning conditions. The illustrated concepts range from volumes and open or enclosed bodies to sequences of interior rooms within a volume.
uses: Relating free space and building volume
Arranging interior rooms within a building volume

fichas.title: Topography: building and site
fichas.summary: Topography refers to a building’s unique location and the town-planning or landscape-related statement developed from it. This site relationship significantly influences the quality of public space. The illustrated approaches include raising a building on columns, forming a hollow beneath its volume, and using a plateau or plinth zone.
uses: Responding to site and landscape conditions
Creating space beneath or around a building

fichas.title: Architectural elements and facade openings
fichas.summary: Structural elements should be designed in keeping with the building’s overall appearance while meeting technical and utility requirements. Openings create a graphical structure on the wall surface; mixing structural principles can produce an overloaded facade. Illustrated approaches include point-type openings, ribbon windows, surface structuring, and wall panels with columns.

fichas.title: Plastic elements: cut-outs and projections
fichas.summary: Functional components such as balconies and loggias, as well as columns, form three-dimensional structures that model the wall surface. The overall wall-surface structure should not interfere with these elements. The examples show cut-outs and deepened cavities in the volume, and plastic elements projecting from it.
uses: Creating depth in a building volume

fichas.title: Roof forms as architectural elements
fichas.summary: The roof completes the building as a sculptural whole. Its form is selected in response to the town-planning context and architectural concept. The illustrated approaches include a flat roof, a pitched roof forming a geometrical body, and equal treatment of roof and wall.
uses: Relating roof design to town-planning context and architectural concept
